answer.rationale: The finance mandate of 18% spend reduction cannot be met through the incumbent (who refused repricing). memory_c2 demonstrates the low-cost vendor successfully handled primary supply with fast onboarding and accurate invoicing, directly supporting a switch. memory_c4 shows negotiation recovered margin but the incumbent has already refused this cycle, foreclosing that path. The low-cost vendor quote alone meets the mandate. However, assembly line operates at 94% committed volume with no buffer—delivery disruption creates material downside risk. Switching to the low-cost vendor on a standard_experiment scale (full contract but with 90-day enhanced SPC monitoring and staged volume increase) addresses the mandate while limiting risk exposure during the transition. memory_c3 (second sourcing) is not deployed here because it requires parallel capacity and budget we do not have; memory_c6 (multi-year commitment) conflicts with the one-decision constraint and does not solve the incumbent's pricing refusal.
